intention: A false statement inside a trouble record can be corrected in place — a correction APPENDED beside it, joined to the exact entry it corrects, so a reader of that record sees both the wrong sentence and what is true. A new door on TroubleDevice, `amend`, alongside raise_trouble and clear: it appends to an `amendments` list and edits nothing. Each amendment carries a join key naming which prior entry it corrects (`{"in": "<list>", "at": "<iso timestamp>"}` — every appended entry in this store already carries an `at`, and no entry has an index that survives a later append), the false statement quoted verbatim, what is true instead, and how that was measured. It does NOT change `standing` and does NOT increment `count`.
why: MEASURED, n=2 in one evening, and the record is on disk: troubles/a-clear-carries-a-false-statement-and-the-lane-has-no-door-to-correct-it.json. Both occurrences are false sentences CC wrote into ONE clear's residue clause — (a) 'run_proof still takes a sink argument and the caller still chooses', falsified six lines below the signature I had grepped; (b) 'that voyage's gate is open; nobody has told it', falsified by a PROVED crossing in a commit Akien authored, in the repo I was committing to. Both landed in the part of a closing record nobody re-measures, because the closing record is the artifact that announces measuring is over — and it is the paragraph the next reader trusts most, being the only forward-looking thing in a record about the past. THE LANE HAD NO WAY TO SAY SO. clear() refuses a second all-clear (rightly — it would overwrite what actually fixed it), raise_trouble on the same identity says a fault RETURNED, and nothing says a sentence was wrong when written. What actually happened is the symptom: a NEW trouble identity was raised to carry the correction, so the correction now lives in a different file from the sentence it corrects, and a reader of the false clear has no route to it. The joining is the whole feature.
traces_to: Law 7 — 'Errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth. A presentation surface may collapse an error into a coherent shape; a record of truth never may.' The trouble store is a record of truth by its own charter (laws.law_7: 'the RECORD is never damped'), and today a false sentence in one is permanent in the wrong direction: it cannot be removed, which is right, and it also cannot be answered, which is not. Also Law 3 — a correction carrying how it was measured is a measurement; one carrying a paragraph is a hypothesis wearing a fix's clothes.

falsifier: DONE when a false statement inside a CLEARED trouble is corrected through the lane's own door and a reader of that record sees both sentences joined — proved three ways, and the second is the one that matters: (a) an amendment on a live and on a cleared trouble both land and both resolve their join key; (b) a tooth shows the amend leaves `standing`, `count`, and the corrected entry's TEXT byte-identical — the door cannot erase, which is the property trust cannot substitute for; (c) an amendment whose join key names no existing entry is REFUSED, so the store cannot gain a floating paragraph. WRONG INTENT if amend becomes a way to make a wrong clear look right: a record carrying an amendment must read as MORE marked than one without, never less. Also wrong if it blurs into the re-raise path — a fault that returned is a new ticket at count 1 by the charter's own words, and an amendment must be structurally unable to say that.

distinctions_recorded: AN INACCURATE RECORD AND A RETURNED FAULT ARE DIFFERENT EVENTS, and the lane can currently express only the second. The charter's clause — 'a fault that returns after a clear is a NEW ticket at count 1, carrying the fix that did not hold' — is exactly right about faults and simply was never about sentences. Tonight the raise door was used to carry a correction anyway, which is the measured symptom rather than a counterexample. The boundary is physics in the design, not manners: amend touches neither `standing` nor `count`, so it is structurally unable to say a fault returned.

THE PRECEDENT IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE CAUSE. validation_store's verdict_change records that a standing MOVED because the world moved — a source fingerprint expired, a seal stopped holding. This records that a SENTENCE WAS WRONG WHEN WRITTEN, and nothing about the world changed. Same append-beside shape, opposite causes, and collapsing the two would make 'the record changed' unable to say why. The borrow is of the pattern and is cited; no bytes move (a graft would need its own ticket and proof).

THIS FIXES THE RECORD AND NOT THE REACH, and the hole is carried knowingly rather than discovered later. An amendment on a CLEARED trouble reaches no standing surface: the SessionStart hook renders live(), and a cleared record is not in it. The design is only worth building if a record that can be read correctly LATER is worth having even when nothing pushes it at anyone — and it is, because a trouble is shareable provenance in git, greppable in fifty years by the charter's own framing. If that is rejected, the answer is a reach ticket, not a bigger amend. The watch counts exactly this, so the question becomes evidence.

NOTHING IN THIS DESIGN TELLS THE AMENDER THAT A CORRECTION IS OWED. Both occurrences were caught because CC happened to re-measure a paragraph it had already written; a false sentence nobody re-reads stays false, and the door changes nothing about that. The door makes a correction POSSIBLE and cheap. Making one NOTICED is a different problem and is not claimed here.
